claim_text: Karachi Port and Port Qasim together handle approximately 90% of Pakistan's external/seaborne trade
source: Pakistan Single Window / Paradigm Shift analysis (multiple outlets)

claim_text: Over 95% of Pakistan's total trade volume moves by sea
Individual Karachi Port / Port Qasim trade-share percentages vary across sources (54-64% and 35-51% respectively) and do not reconcile
Karachi Port Trust FY2024-25 cargo throughput was 53.95 million tons (138-year record) - 41.68 million tons dry cargo + 12.28 million tons liquid bulk + 2.65 million TEUs containers
source: Profit by Pakistan Today / Business Recorder / Arab News / Dawn / Bloom Pakistan

claim_text: Karachi Port Trust FY2025-26 cargo throughput rose to 55.44 million tons (up 2.76% year-on-year)
source: Profit by Pakistan Today / Business Recorder

claim_text: Port Qasim FY2024-25 grand total cargo throughput was 45.305 million tonnes (13.48M dry + 19.091M liquid + 12.734M container by weight)
source: Port Qasim Authority official port-performance page

claim_text: Combined Karachi Port + Port Qasim FY2024-25 throughput is approximately 99.3 million tonnes
source: Claude's addition of C004 and C006

claim_text: Gwadar Port cargo throughput was 34000 tonnes in 2024 down from 592000 tonnes in 2023
Gwadar has handled a cumulative total of 4789 containers since operations began against an installed annual capacity of 240000 TEUs
source: government statement to National Assembly cited by press

claim_text: Gwadar's second-phase development was handed to China Overseas Port Holding Company (COPHC) in February 2013
source: Middle East Institute / general CPEC history sources

claim_text: COPHC invested approximately $1.62 billion in Gwadar port development; a second reported $1.62 billion Phase II figure may be a duplicate of the same figure rather than a separate tranche
Broader CPEC investment pledges grew from an initial ~$46 billion to ~$62 billion roughly one-fifth of Pakistan's GDP at the time
Gwadar's deep-water port became formally operational in 2016 a decade after first-phase construction completed with three berths and initial installed capacity of 137000 containers per year
source: Charter Cities Institute / general CPEC history sources

claim_text: In 2017 Gwadar port received only 145 TEUs of project cargo and no general commercial cargo vessel that year
source: Digital Logistics Capacity Assessments / general CPEC history sources

claim_text: Gwadar Free Zone Phase 1 has approximately 47 enterprises registered (6 factories built, 3 fully operational); a separate figure describes 35 companies registered in Free Zone South with 9 fully operational
source: Graana.com / Zameen.com Gwadar Free Zone guides

claim_text: Minimum investment to register in Gwadar Free Zone is $500000 plus a $3000 registration fee

The M-8 motorway (Gwadar-Ratodero, 892km planned) remains only partially built; Gwadar-Hoshab (193km) opened February 2016; Hoshab-Awaran under construction as of 2025 with over Rs25 billion allocated
A direct Gwadar rail link (Gwadar-Mastung and Besima-Jacobabad) is a mid-term CPEC project scheduled to begin in 2025 and conclude by 2030

In December 2024 Pakistan's Parliamentary Secretary for Planning told the National Assembly Gwadar was fully operational and equipped to handle all kinds of cargo, contradicting the 34000-tonne 2024 throughput figure

A report submitted to PM Shehbaz Sharif on Gwadar operationalization identified barriers: security concerns/insurance costs, high operational costs, lack of infrastructure, limited international interest

In 2026 Gwadar's cargo activity increased sharply: approximately 11000 containers processed in April 2026 alone (more than all of 2025's ~8300 TEUs), and approximately 200000 tonnes of transit breakbulk cargo over three months, linked by reporting to Hormuz shipping disruption
